messages:
maya: Customer reported intermittent 403s + 300-600ms tail latency for requests that appear to be routed to eu-west instead of us-west. customer says it started ~1h ago.

liam: I see a spike in cross-region egress and a series of failed healthchecks from the us-west pool around 1769903500 — health status flipped to UNHEALTHY and failover kicked in.

olivia: Any recent changes to probe sources or LB config? :thinking:

jordan: Rolled the probe-pool rotation yesterday to move probes to the new GCLB pool (see internal doc link). New pool uses IP range 35.203.0.0/16. Could be firewall whitelist issue.

maya: Customer sent sample request ids — responses show 403 from edge, then timeouts to model endpoints. Attaching short log excerpt below.

liam: Heartbeat logs (snippet):
```
2026-06-02T12:44:11Z probe-src=35.203.45.12 path=/_health status=RST
2026-06-02T12:44:12Z probe-src=34.102.0.5 path=/_health status=200
2026-06-02T12:44:13Z probe-src=35.203.45.12 path=/_health status=RST
```

olivia: That looks like the probe TCP was being reset (RST) by something on the customer side. If the health agent sees repeated RSTs, it marks the node unhealthy -> triggers failover.

jordan: Can we confirm the external probe source for the customer? maya, can you ask them to run this from their control plane and paste the output:
`curl -vS --resolve api.redwood:443:34.68.10.12 https://api.redwood/_probe`

maya: Customer ran it and reported source IP 35.203.45.12 and then immediate RST. They confirmed they have an IP whitelist for probes that hasn't been updated.

jordan: Temporary mitigation — re-enable old probe pool for the affected LB and pause automatic failover for acme-inc route while customer updates whitelist. infra-bot: initiating rollback of probe-pool-rotation for cluster-usw2.

infra-bot: action: rollback probe-pool change initiated by @jordan — ETA ~5m.

liam: After rollback / whitelist update we saw healthchecks succeed and nodes marked healthy again. This was a false-negative healthcheck causing cross-region failover, not underlying model node failure.

olivia: Support runbook for this case (short):
1) Confirm probe source IP seen by customer (curl test).
2) If RST/blocked, ask customer to add GCLB probe CIDR 35.203.0.0/16 to whitelist OR request temporary fallback to old probe pool.
3) Pause failover for impacted route until stable for 24h.
4) Open infra ticket to document and communicate probe-pool rotations.
Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/health-probe-ip-whitelist

maya: Customer added whitelist entry and re-tested. Traffic stayed in us-west, latency returned to normal. They asked about possible billing credits for the cross-region spike — forwarding to finance.

jordan: Created INFRA-4821 to update rollout docs and add a pre-rollout customer-comms step for probe IP changes.

liam: TL;DR: root cause = probe source IP pool change + customer IP whitelist -> false-negative healthcheck -> cross-region failover. Fix = whitelist CIDR or restore old probe source; added runbook + infra ticket. :white_check_mark:
